narrativeContractAuthority: Declared by the player; it outranks whatever you infer from state and memory. Only the [Main cast] listed below may drive this turn; anyone not listed who has barely appeared recently is background at most — never the centre of a scene, never the emotional turn, never promoted to a new lead:
narrativeContractPeripheralRule: Listed characters who have not appeared recently need not be dragged in either.
characterVectorHeader: [Character Vectors] Where these characters are currently moving in the protagonist's story. A heading is a tendency, not an ending: they only try to move this way, and the scene and the dice decide; both sides of a tension are real and which prevails is decided by this moment's scene — never turn it into a rule; vectors shift with the plot and can flip when a truth comes out; only this turn's relevant characters are listed. The world keeps nobody's secret and reveals nobody's secret: characters act on what they know and want, the protagonist infers from what the protagonist has seen, the narration writes only what the protagonist can perceive.
characterVectorUnconfirmedLabel: [Unconfirmed by the protagonist] Used only to keep world-side action consistent; the person concerned does not explain it, reassure with it or spell it out, and the narration does not write it as known inside the protagonist's viewpoint; whether the protagonist can think of it depends only on what the protagonist has seen — never close that door for the protagonist, never confirm it for them:
